doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

chapter: Teenage obsession and the record store
title: Parents, the family store and the start-up loan
summary: His parents wanted a doctor or lawyer but ran a small retail store; his father gave him a lump sum to start a business.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: If you had had a discussion with your parents about 13 or 14, the old “What do you want to do when you grow up?” How would that have gone at that point?

I wouldn’t have had much of an answer for them. I didn’t know what my future was going to be and in fact my parents hoped, you know, I would become a doctor or a lawyer and all of those things. But they had no clue how to orient themselves to guiding me in that direction. My dad owned a small business, a retail store. My mother did the books. And they did not set me out on this path to be an intellectual or a doctor or a lawyer, they even told me to take Latin and it might help me to become a doctor. But it did the opposite. So eventually I followed exactly in the footsteps of my dad and became a retailer rather than a lawyer, doctor, or scholar.
Didn’t he give you a jumpstart on that with a loan saying —

He did. He did. He said, “Jerry, here’s X amount of money you can start a business, you can continue with schooling, you must rent an apartment and get the hell out of here.” So it was a lump sum “get out of here and you figure it out.” It was like that.
